quotes.text: And so, we're joining folks like Rep. Pearson down there in Tennessee and other folks across the nation on a moratorium, because, in reality, there's states that either don't have any laws on the books, have weak laws on the books. And in reality, what's happening is these big corporations are coming in, bullying our local communities. [...] And so, we do need a moratorium. But in reality, we need to make sure that these are union jobs and that, like, at the end of the day, people's environmental justice is protected.

But in Michigan, we put some protections in there — doesn't necessarily go far enough, but at least we have some guardrails on there saying that if you take taxpayer dollars or if you're taking our tax credits here in our state, then you have to create a closed-loop system and, you know, protecting people's water and their electrical grid. But it doesn't go far enough.
